At will: animal friendship (snakes only), poison spray
3/day: suggestion

npcs.description: Sekelok is a tall, muscular yuan-ti pureblood. He has the statistics of a champion (see appendix D), with these changes: Sekelok is neutral evil. He wears no armor, but his scales are as hard as steel (AC 18). He is immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition. He has darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. He speaks Abyssal, Common, and Draconic. He has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. He has the Innate Spellcasting trait described below.

npcs.name: Azi Mas

features.name: Awakened
features.description: Long ago, a jungle druid used an awaken spell on Azi Mas, giving him an intelligence of 10 and the ability to speak Common.

features.name: Good Memory
features.description: Azi Mas has a good memory; he can remember names and faces and is quick to warn his masters if yuan-ti pass through whom he hasn't seen before.

npcs.description: Azi Mas is a snake that was awakened by a jungle druid. He remains coiled in the shadows, is bored, and enjoys chatting with yuan-ti visitors. Should other creatures enter from the southwest, Azi Mas ambushes them and tries to take a hostage. If outmatched, he whines and pleads for mercy.

npcs.name: Xopal

features.name: Bronze Syringe
features.description: Xopal carries a bronze syringe containing three doses of a poison cocktail. As an action, he can make a melee weapon attack with the syringe (+3 to hit), which deals 1 piercing damage and injects one dose of poison on a hit. Any creature injected with a dose of poison must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. In addition, the creature is poisoned for 1 hour whether or not its save succeeds.

actions.name: Bronze Syringe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1 piercing damage and injects one dose of poison. Any creature injected with a dose of poison must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. In addition, the creature is poisoned for 1 hour whether or not its save succeeds.

npcs.description: Xopal is a yuan-ti pureblood who bottles and blends venom to create deadly new strains. He believes it's his destiny to transform into a much more powerful form of yuan-ti—a metamorphosis that will occur when he develops a poison so virulent that even innate immunity to poison can't withstand it. He uses zombies as test subjects; once he's overcome their immunity, he plans to conduct further tests on live yuan-ti.

npcs.name: Withers

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description:
Withers is a 9th-level spellcaster. His spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 13; +5 to hit with spell attacks). He has the following wizard spells prepared:
Cantrips (at will): acid splash, mage hand, minor illusion, prestidigitation
1st level (4 slots): detect magic, expeditious retreat, featherfall, thunderwave
2nd level (3 slots): darkness, hold person, rope trick
3rd level (3 slots): dispel magic, lightning bolt
4th level (3 slots): blight, wall of fire
5th level (1 slot): telekinesis

actions.name: Battleaxe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8+2) slashing damage, or 7 (1d10+2) slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Life Drain
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 5 (1d6+2) necrotic damage. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

npcs.description: Withers was an Omuan engineer named Gorra before he was turned into an undead creature. He is fiercely loyal to Acererak and his passion for learning followed him into undeath.
npcs.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.143

npcs.name: Artus Cimber

features.name: Special Equipment
features.description: Artus wears the Ring of Winter. He and the ring can't be targeted by divination magic or perceived through magical scrying sensors. While attuned to and wearing the ring, Artus ceases to age and is immune to cold damage and the effects of extreme cold. Artus wields Bookmark, a +3 dagger with additional magical properties. As a bonus action, Artus can activate any one of the following properties while attuned to the dagger, provided he has the weapon drawn: • Cause a blue gem set into the dagger's pommel to shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet, or make the gem go dark. • Turn the dagger into a compass that, while resting on Artus's palm, points north. • Cast dimension door from the dagger. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn. • Cast i;ompulsion (save DC 15) from the dagger. The range of the spell increases to 90 feet, but the spell targets only spiders that are beasts. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Artus makes three attacks with Bookmark or his longbow.

actions.name: Bookmark (+3 Dagger)
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d4 + 5) piercing damage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) piercing damage.

actions.name: Ring of Winter
actions.description: The Ring of Winter has 12 charges and regains all its expended charges daily at dawn. While attuned to and wearing the ring, Artus can expend the necessary number of charges to activate one of the following properties: • Artus can expend 1 charge and use the ring to lower the temperature In a 120-foot-radius sphere centered on a point he can see within 300 feet of him. The temperature in that area drops 20 degrees per minute, to a minimum of - 30 degrees Fahrenheit. Frost and ice begin to form ol1 surfaces once the temperature drops below 32 degrees. This effect is permanent unless Artus uses the ring to end the effect as an action, at which point the temperature in the area returns to normal at a rate of 10 degrees per minute. • Artus can cast one of the following spells from the ring (spell save DC 17) by expending the necessary number of charges: Bigby's hand (2 charges; the hand is made of ice, is immune to cold damage, and deals bludgeoning damage instead of force damage as a clenched fist), cone of cold (2 charges), flesh to ice (3 charges; as flesh to stone except that the target turns to solid ice with the density and durability of stone), ice storm {2 charges), Otiluke'sfreezing sphere (3 charges), sleet storm (1 charge), spike growth (1 charge; the spikes are made of ice), or wall of ice (2 charges). • Artus can expend the necessary number of charges and use the ring to create either an inanimate ice object (2 charges) or an animated ice creature (4 charges). The ice object can't have any moving parts, must be able to fit inside a 10-foot cube, and has the density and durability of metal or stone (Artus's choice). The ice creature must be modeled after a beast with a challenge rating of 2 or less. The ice creature has the same statistics as the beast it models, with the following changes: the creature is a construct with vulnerability to fire damage, immunity to cold and poison damage, and immunity to the following conditions: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, and poisoned. The ice creature obeys only its creator's commands. The ice object or creature appears in an unoccupied space within 60 feet of Artus. It melts into a pool of normal water after 24 hours or when it drops to 0 hit points. In extreme heat, it loses 5 (ldlO) hit points per minute as it melts. Use the guidelines in chapter 8 of the Dungeon Master's Guide to determine the hit points of an inanimate object if they become necessary.

npcs.description: A former member of the Harpers, Artus Cimber is the keeper of the Ring of Winter. He found the ring in the jungles of Chult, where he also met his wife, Alisaoda. The ring halts its wearer's natural aging and has allowed Artus to survive well beyond his natural lifespan. The ring also defies magical attempts to divine its location and that of its weare r. On his fingers above the knuckles, Artus has tattooed the names of his dearly departed animal companions- a pair of talking wombats named Byrt and Lugg.

npcs.name: Mwaxanare

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description:
Mwaxanare is a 2nd-level spellcaster. Her spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 13, +5 to hit with spell attacks). She regains her expended spell slots when she finishes a short or long rest. She knows the following warlock spells:
Cantrips (at will): eldritch blast, mage hand
1st level (2 slots): charm person, protection from evil and good, unseen servant

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 2 (1d4) piercing damage.

npcs.description: At the tender age of seventeen, Princess Mwaxanare ("Nana" for short) is the oldest living descendant of the royal families of Omu and the natural inheritor of their fallen kingdom. She and her six-year-old brother, Na, are guests of the aarakocra in Kir Sabal.

npcs.name: Ras Nsi

features.name: Ideal
features.description: "I seek to bring about the end of this world and rule the next one."

features.name: Bond
features.description: "The yuan-ti of Chult are mine to command. They will help me rule an empire."

features.name: Flaw
features.description: "I will do anything and betray anyone to save myself."

actions.name: Constrict
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 14). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and Ras Nsi can't constrict another target.

actions.name: Flame Tongue Longsword (Yuan-ti Form Only)
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) slashing damage, or 8 (1d10 + 3) slashing damage when used with two hands, plus 7 (2d6) fire damage.

npcs.description: Ras Nsi is a yuan-ti leader who seeks to bring about the end of the world and rule the next one.

npcs.name: Volothamp "Volo" Geddarm

features.name: Spellcasting
features.description:
Volo is a 1st-level spellcaster. His spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 12, +4 to hit with spell attacks). He has the following wizard spells prepared:
Cantrips (at will): friends, mending, prestidigitation
1st level (2 slots): comprehend languages, detect magic, disguise self

actions.name: Dagger
actions.description: Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing damage.

npcs.description: The bombastic world traveler Volothamp Geddarm has come to Chult to deliver signed copies of his latest book, Volo's Guide to Monsters.

backgrounds.name: Anthropologist

feature.name: Adept Linguist
feature.description: You can communicate with humanoids who don't speak any language you know. You must observe the humanoids interacting with one another for at least 1 day, after which you learn a handful of important words, expressions, and gestures-enough to communicate on a rudimentary level.

backgrounds.description: You have always been fascinated by other cultures, from the most ancient and primeval lost lands to the most modern civilizations. By studying other cultures' customs, philosophies, laws, rituals, religious beliefs, languages, and art, you have learned how tribes, empires, and all forms of society in between craft their own destinies and doom. This knowledge came to you not only through books and scrolls, but also through first-hand observation- by visiting far-flung settlements and exploring local histories and customs.

backgrounds.name: Cultural Chameleon

feature.name: Adept Linguist
feature.description: You can communicate with humanoids who don't speak any language you know. You must observe the humanoids interacting with one another for at least 1 day, after which you learn a handful of important words, expressions, and gestures-enough to communicate on a rudimentary level.

backgrounds.description: Before becoming an adventurer, you spent much of your adult life away from your homeland, living among people different from your kin. You came to understand these foreign cultures and the ways of their people, who eventually treated you as one of their own. One culture had more of an influence on you than any other, shaping your beliefs and customs. Choose a race whose culture you've adopted, or roll on the Adopted Culture table.

backgrounds.name: Archaeologist
equipment: A wooden case containing a map to a ruin or dungeon
a trinket recovered from a dig site

feature.name: Historical Knowledge
feature.description: When you enter a ruin or dungeon, you can correctly ascertain its original purpose and determine its builders, whether those were dwarves, elves, humans, yuan-ti, or some other known race. In addition, you can determine the monetary value of art objects more than a century old.

backgrounds.description: An archaeologist learns about the long-lost and fallen cultures of the past by studying their remains-their bones, their ruins, their surviving masterworks, and their tombs. Those who practice archaeology travel to the far corners of the world to root through crumbled cities and lost dungeons, digging in search of artifacts that might tell the stories of monarchs and high priests, wars and cataclysms.

traps.name: Concealed Pit Trap
traps.trigger: An individual who crosses this section of floor has a 50 percent chance of triggering the trapdoor and dropping into the 20-foot-deep pit.

detection.detail: Attempts to spot this pit trap are made with disadvantage due to the thick layer of mud, creepers, and blown-in leaves covering the stone-tiled floor.

traps.effect: The trapdoor opens, dropping the creature into a 20-foot-deep pit, taking damage from the fall as normal. Once the pit opens, a narrow ledge remains around the outside edge. The ledge can be traversed safely with a successful DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, but a character with someone riding on his or her shoulders makes the check with disadvantage.
traps.description: A concealed pit trap with a trapdoor hidden under mud, creepers, and leaves, dropping victims into a 20-foot-deep pit.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.45

traps.name: Blade Trap
traps.trigger: Each individual that passes through this section of the corridor has a 50 percent chance of triggering scything blades that sweep out from concealed wall niches.

detection.detail: Once identified, the trap can be jammed by hammering spikes or metal blades into the niches.

disarm.method: Strength checks (hammering spikes or metal blades into the niches)
disarm.detail: Once identified, the trap can be jammed by hammering spikes or metal blades into the niches and succeeding on four separate DC 10 Strength checks (to hammer in the metal solidly enough). Each successful check jams one scythe and reduces the trap's damage by 1d8.

traps.effect: Scything blades sweep out from concealed wall niches. Any creature in the 10-foot-square section of hall between the blades must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 18 (4d8) slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: 10-foot-square section of hall between the blades
traps.description: A corridor trap with concealed wall niches that release scything blades when triggered.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.45

traps.name: Puzzle Floor
traps.trigger: If an individual applies more than a few pounds of pressure to any square except the one corresponding to the lit-up square on the door, magical flames blast out from the walls.

detection.detail: Even if someone can see that area of the door, the glow is so faint that a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check is needed to notice it.

disarm.detail: This trigger and trap are magical, so they can't be disarmed or jammed mechanically. Casting dispel magic on the floor tiles disables the trap for 1 hour.

traps.effect: Magical flames blast out from the walls. Every creature on the terrace when the flames appear must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: The terrace (16-foot-high terrace with tiled floor)
traps.description: A tiled floor puzzle where stepping on the wrong square triggers magical flames from the walls.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.45

traps.name: Puzzle Door Glyph
traps.trigger: If wrong squares are pressed, the squares are pressed in the wrong order, or they're pressed by the wrong people, a glyph of warding on the door triggers a thunderwave spell.

detection.detail: Finding the glyph requires a thorough search of the door and a successful DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

traps.effect: A glyph of warding on the door triggers a thunderwave spell. Every creature on the ledge when the spell triggers must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 9 (2d8) thunder damage, is pushed 10 feet away from the door, and falls into area 6C, setting off the trap there. A creature that succeeds on the save takes half damage and is not pushed.
traps.description: A glyph of warding on a puzzle door that triggers a thunderwave spell when the wrong squares are pressed.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.45

traps.name: Trapped Steps
traps.trigger: Each of steps 3, 10, 17, and 23 has a glyph of warding spell placed on it, set to trigger when the step is walked on. Creatures emulating Man and Crocodile don't trigger the glyphs.

detection.detail: To spot a glyph, the dust on the step must be cleared away, and a character searching the step must succeed on a DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

traps.effect: Each triggered glyph releases a 20-foot-radius sphere of lightning centered on the step. Every creature in the area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (5d8) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Creatures emulating Man and Crocodile have disadvantage on the saving throw.
traps.description: Glyphs of warding on specific steps of a spiral staircase that release lightning when triggered.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.45

traps.name: Falling Bricks
traps.trigger: If the jug is picked up by anyone else (not emulating Man and Crocodile), loose bricks begin to fall from the ceiling.
traps.effect: Every creature in area 6E is struck by falling bricks and must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that starts its turn in the room repeats the saving throw. After 3 rounds, the bricks stop falling.
traps.description: A trap that causes loose bricks to fall from the ceiling when the alchemy jug is picked up improperly.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.45

traps.name: Concealed Pit
traps.trigger: The first character to step on the pit falls in.

detection.detail: The lead character spots the pit with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

traps.effect: The first character to step on a pit falls in, taking 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage and landing on 1d4 stakes, each of which deals 3 (1d6) piercing damage and 7 (2d6) poison damage.
traps.damage: 3 (1d6) bludgeoning plus 1d4 stakes each dealing 3 (1d6) piercing and 7 (2d6) poison
traps.area: 5 feet wide, 10 feet deep, lined with poisoned wooden stakes
traps.description: A concealed pit 5 feet wide, 10 feet deep, and lined with poisoned wooden stakes.
traps.source: Chapter 2: The Land of Chult, p.19

traps.name: Pit Trap
traps.trigger: The first character to step on a pit falls in.

detection.detail: A character spots the pit with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

traps.effect: The first character to step on a pit falls in, taking 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage and landing on 1d4 stakes, each of which deals 3 (1d6) piercing damage and 7 (2d6) poison damage.
traps.damage: 3 (1d6) bludgeoning plus 1d4 stakes each dealing 3 (1d6) piercing and 7 (2d6) poison
traps.description: A hidden pit trap that a character can spot with a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. The first character to step on it falls in, taking bludgeoning damage and landing on stakes that deal piercing and poison damage.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.19

traps.name: Treasury Lower Lock Trap
traps.trigger: The trap is triggered if an attempt to pick the lower lock fails by 5 or more, if the wrong key is used in the lock, or if it's opened by any means before the upper lock.

detection.detail: The trap can be spotted with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: It's impossible to disarm or bypass.

traps.effect: The trap causes the metal gantry between the treasury and the forge (area 4) to retract west, leaving a 40-foot gap across the magma. The bridge can be re-extended only by lifting the lever in the corridor from area 4. The lever is too far away to be manipulated with mage hand by anyone on the treasury side of the magma river.
traps.area: The metal gantry between the treasury and the forge (area 4)
traps.description: A trap on the lower lock of the treasury door that retracts the gantry across the magma river when triggered.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.62

traps.name: Drugged Fruit and Wine
traps.trigger: A character eats or drinks the drugged fruit or wine.

detection.detail: The contamination can be detected only by someone who has proficiency in Medicine and who succeeds on a DC 13 Wisdom (Medicine) check.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

traps.effect: Characters who eat or drink must make a successful DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 hour or until they drink 2 quarts of water.
traps.description: A tray of fruit and wine artfully drugged in Zalkore's lair.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.79

traps.name: Dreaming Tincture
traps.trigger: A character drinks a dose of the tincture.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

traps.effect: On a failed save, the character begins to experience illusory sights, sounds, smells, and sensations that seem real. Casting a lesser restoration spell or similar magic on the character ends the effect, which otherwise lasts for 1d4 + 4 hours.
traps.description: A tincture found in Zalkore's lair that causes hallucinations when consumed.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.80

traps.name: Rolling Stone Trap
traps.trigger: A tripwire stretches across the mouth of the tunnel where the lower passage joins the cart track. If the tripwire is missed, each character who passes through the tunnel mouth has a 50 percent chance to trip it and trigger two mechanisms.

detection.detail: It can be spotted with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.

traps.effect: The first mechanism is a spring-loaded wooden contraption resembling a claw that swings out from the wall of the mine shaft up-slope from this tunnel to snap across the tunnel mouth. Whoever triggered the trap must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity throw or take 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage from the claw. One round later, the second mechanism releases a 5-foot-diameter stone sphere that drops into the cave (marked T on the map) and rolls into the wooden claw across the tunnel mouth, which is demolished by the sphere's impact-but not before diverting the sphere onto the cart tracks. The sphere careens down the tracks until it reaches area 11, where it derails and smashes into the urds' living quarters. (The urds easily hear it coming and get out of the way.) Everyone in the sphere's path must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. Instead of being hit by the sphere, a character who fails the saving throw can opt to leap off the tracks and fall to the bottom of the shaft; this succeeds automatically. The sphere can't be slowed down by Strength checks because of the steep incline of the tracks.
traps.damage: 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage from the claw; 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage from the sphere
traps.area: The tunnel mouth and the cart tracks down to area 11
traps.description: A tripwire triggers a spring-loaded claw and then a rolling stone sphere that careens down the tracks.
traps.source: Chapter 2, p.87

traps.name: Swinging Log Trap
traps.trigger: A character moving through the passage has a 50 percent chance to trip the trigger wire.

detection.detail: can be spotted with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check

traps.effect: Each creature in the passage when the log swings through must make a successful DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 10 (3d6) piercing damage and be knocked prone.
traps.description: A swinging log studded with spikes traps the north passage connecting this chamber to the cart track.
traps.source: Chapter 2, p.87

traps.name: Tripwire Alarm
traps.trigger: Approaching enemies trigger a tripwire.

detection.detail: Notice the tripwires with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check; otherwise, they're noticed by anyone with a passive Wisdom (Perception) score of 13 or higher.

traps.effect: If approaching enemies are noticed by sentries or trigger a tripwire, the village goes on alert, making it impossible to sneak in.
traps.description: A tripwire alarm that alerts the village when triggered.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.90

traps.name: Village Launch Mechanism
traps.trigger: Cutting the thick vine.

detection.detail: A character who gets a good look at the village in daylight and succeeds on a DC 18 Wisdom (Perception) check spots the network of vines and the bent tree and recognizes them as a gigantic spring trap. Those with proficiency in the Survival skill have advantage on this check.

traps.effect: The village is launched. Anyone inside the net when the village is launched and hits the ground must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 28 (8d6) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.description: A gigantic spring trap that launches the village.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.90

traps.name: Poison Gas Trap (Shagambi's Shrine Pedestal)
traps.trigger: Any physical attempt to force open the stone hatch in the top of the pedestal

detection.detail: With a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check, a character notices tiny holes in the relief. Stuffing the holes with cloth or wax prevents the poison gas from penetrating through when the pedestal is disturbed.

disarm.method: Stuffing the holes with cloth or wax
disarm.detail: Stuffing the holes with cloth or wax prevents the poison gas from penetrating through when the pedestal is disturbed.

traps.effect: A cloud of gas releases through the holes in the wall relief. The gas fills a 15-foot cube directly in front of the mural. Creatures in the area must make a DC 12 Constitution saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) poison damage on a failed saving throw, or half as much damage on a successful one. The gas affects a creature even if it holds its breath or doesn't need to breathe. The gas doesn't linger.
traps.area: 15-foot cube directly in front of the mural
traps.description: A poison gas trap triggered by forcing open the stone hatch on the pedestal in Shagambi's shrine, releasing gas through tiny holes in the wall relief.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.100

traps.name: Covered Pit Trap
traps.trigger: A creature stepping on a pit cover causes it to swing open and falls in unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. The covers remain locked until the puzzle cube is moved from the pedestal in area 6C.

detection.detail: A character who searches the hallway floor for traps finds a pit trap with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.method: magic such as an arcane lock spell
disarm.detail: The lids are cleverly constructed and can be jammed shut only by using magic such as an arcane lock spell.

traps.effect: A creature stepping on a pit cover causes it to swing open and falls in unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. Each pit is 10 feet deep and has a patch of green slime (see chapter 5 of the Dungeon Master's Guide) at the bottom of it.
traps.area: Three covered pits spaced along the corridor in the positions marked X on the shrine map.
traps.description: Three covered pits are spaced along the corridor. Their covers remain locked until the puzzle cube is moved from the pedestal in area 6C. Each pit is 10 feet deep and has a patch of green slime at the bottom.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.123

traps.name: Unkh's Shrine Pedestal Trap
traps.trigger: A character inserts the wrong key into the keyhole at the base of the pedestal or botches an attempt to pick the lock (fails the DC 25 Dexterity check by 5 or more).

detection.detail: No detection method specified in the source text.

disarm.detail: Using thieves' tools, a character can pick the lock on the pedestal with a successful DC 25 Dexterity check. A character who fails the check by 5 or more accidentally triggers the trap.

traps.effect: The shell of the flail snail statue emits dazzling rays of light that fire in all directions. Each creature in the shrine must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw. Any creature that fails the save is struck by a ray and takes 33 (6d10) radiant damage. The statue can't emit rays while wholly or partly contained within an antimagic field.
traps.description: A trap on the pedestal in Unkh's shrine that fires dazzling rays of light from the flail snail statue when the wrong key is inserted or the lock is botched.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.103

traps.name: Poison Darts
traps.trigger: If more than 20 pounds of pressure is exerted on the wrong picture tile, four poison darts shoot from holes in the walls.

detection.detail: A character can spot the holes with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.method: Stuffing the holes with cloth or wax
disarm.detail: Stuffing the holes with cloth or wax prevents the darts from launching.

traps.effect: Four poison darts shoot from holes in the walls. Each dart makes a ranged weapon attack (+5 to hit) against a random target within 10 feet of the triggering tile. A single creature can be attacked by multiple darts. A creature hit by a dart takes 2 (1d4) piercing damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 7 (2d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: A 20-foot-long, 10-foot-wide stretch of the hallway, within 10 feet of the triggering tile
traps.description: A trap of poison darts hidden in the walls of a hallway tiled with beast carvings, triggered by stepping on the same animal more than once.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.103

traps.name: Axe Blade Trap
traps.trigger: If more than 20 pounds of pressure is exerted on a pressure plate, a sharpened axe blade swings from a hidden compartment in the ceiling.

detection.detail: A character searching for traps spots a pressure plate and ceiling compartment with a successful DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: Wedging an iron spike or other object under a plate prevents the trap from triggering. Using thieves' tools, a character can dismantle an axe blade with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. If the check fails by 5 or more, the trap triggers and makes an attack against the character with disadvantage.

traps.effect: The blade makes a melee attack (+6 to hit) against any creature standing on the pressure plate. On a hit, the target takes 8 (1d8 + 4) slashing damage.
traps.area: Any creature standing on the pressure plate
traps.description: Hidden pressure plates in the floor trigger a sharpened axe blade from the ceiling in a dusty maze.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.103

traps.name: Puzzle Cube Trap
traps.trigger: Any creature that touches the puzzle cube

disarm.detail: When the torches in this room are inserted into the empty brackets in area 19B, Obo'laka's puzzle cube can be handled safely.

traps.effect: Any creature that touches the puzzle cube must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be petrified. Even on a success, a creature holding the cube must repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns until the puzzle cube is removed from the shrine.
traps.description: A magical trap on a puzzle cube that petrifies creatures that touch it.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.109

traps.name: Soporific Gas Trap
traps.trigger: Pressing the stone button (black opal) in Ras Nsi's crown on the wall relief

detection.detail: A character who searches the reliefs and succeeds on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check discovers that the black opal in Ras Nsi's crown is a stone button. If the check succeeds by 5 or more, the character also sees tiny holes hidden among the scales of the Night Serpent carvings.

disarm.method: Plug the holes with cloth or wax
disarm.detail: Using cloth or wax, characters can plug the hundreds of holes and prevent the gas from flowing out.

traps.effect: The carvings of the Night Serpent expel a soporific gas that fills the hallway and lingers for 1 minute. Any creature that moves into the gas or starts its turn inside it must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. The gas has no effect on creatures that cannot be poisoned, and creatures that fail the save fall unconscious for 1 hour.
traps.description: A hidden button in a wall relief triggers a soporific gas that fills the hallway, knocking creatures unconscious.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.115

traps.name: Poison Needle Trap
traps.trigger: A character who tries to pick the lock without first disabling the trap

detection.detail: Finding the trap requires a successful DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check

disarm.detail: once found, it can be disabled with a successful DC 12 Dexterity check

traps.effect: The character is pricked by the needle, takes 5 (1d10) poison damage, and is blinded. The blindness is permanent but can be cured with a lesser restoration spell or similar magic.
traps.area: The lock on the south door
traps.description: The south door is locked, and the lock contains a cleverly hidden poison needle trap.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.122

traps.name: False Entrance Gas Trap
traps.trigger: Inserting puzzle cubes representing every trickster god except Unkh into the cavities in such a way that the cubes of rival gods are opposite to one another causes a stone block to slowly descend over the tunnel entrance.

detection.detail: Any character searching the tunnel for traps spots the raised stone block with a successful DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.method: Dexterity check (six successful checks, each made as an action)
disarm.detail: Stuffing the holes in the mouths of the skulls with cloth or wax prevents the gas from being released. Doing so while the trap is active is difficult, requiring six successful DC 10 Dexterity checks, each made as an action.

traps.effect: A stone block slowly descends over the tunnel entrance. Any character in the tunnel must decide whether to stay or to flee, which requires a successful DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check. Characters who stay or who fail the check are trapped when the stone block seals off the tunnel. Once the tunnel is sealed, caustic gas billows out from the mouths of the relief-carved skulls. Any creature trapped in the tunnel must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 5 (1d10) poison damage and 5 (1d10) acid damage. While any affected creature remains in the tunnel, it must repeat the saving throw at the start of each of its turns. After 10 rounds, the gas valves close and the stone block rises back into the ceiling. Any puzzle cubes still in their cavities are pushed out, and the trap resets.
traps.area: The tunnel of the false entrance
traps.description: A false entrance to the Tomb of the Nine Gods that seals with a stone block and releases caustic gas when the wrong combination of puzzle cubes is inserted.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.145

traps.name: First Puzzle Door
traps.trigger: A puzzle cube is placed incorrectly in one of the nine cube-shaped cavities.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of evocation magic around each of the cavities.

disarm.detail: The door opens only when all nine puzzle cubes are placed in the proper configuration. A mage hand spell can be used to place the cubes from farther away and avoid the damage.

traps.effect: If a puzzle cube is placed incorrectly, any previously placed cubes pop out. Electricity then erupts from the incorrectly placed cube, dealing 18 (4d8) lightning damage to any creature within 20 feet of the door.
traps.description: A slab of worked stone blocks the overgrown tunnel some twenty feet from the entrance. Grinning skulls mark the edges of the slab, in the center of which are nine cube-shaped cavities arranged in three rows of three. The cubes representing the trickster gods must be placed so that each god is opposite its rival's cube on the grid, with Unkh (who is neutral and has no rivals) in the middle.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.132

traps.name: Pit Trap (Second Puzzle Door)
traps.trigger: Pulling the lever causes the floor between the two doors to split open along a central seam.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: The pit remains open until the lever is reset to its original position.

traps.effect: Each creature standing on the floor when the lever is pulled tumbles into a 20-foot-deep pit lined with poisoned spikes. With a successful DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, the character who pulled the lever can avoid falling by hanging onto it.
traps.damage: 11 (2d10) bludgeoning damage and impaled on 1d4 spikes, each of which deals 3 (1d6) piercing damage and 5 (1d10) poison damage
traps.description: A pit trap triggered by pulling a lever, causing the floor to split open and drop creatures into a spiked pit.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.132

traps.name: Pit Trap (Lever-Operated)
traps.trigger: A character pulls a lever, causing the pit to open. The character who pulled the lever can avoid falling by hanging onto it with a successful DC 15 Dexterity saving throw.

detection.detail: Spotting the seam along the floor requires a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: Characters can hammer spikes into the floor to prevent it from dropping, but at least ten spikes are needed because of the floor's size and weight.

traps.effect: The pit remains open until the lever is reset to its original position. Each creature falling into the pit takes 11 (2d10) bludgeoning damage and is impaled on 1d4 spikes, each of which deals 3 (1d6) piercing damage and 5 (1d10) poison damage. Any creature that takes poison damage from one or more spikes is poisoned for 24 hours, or until the condition is removed with a lesser restoration spell or similar magic.
traps.damage: 11 (2d10) bludgeoning plus 1d4 spikes each dealing 3 (1d6) piercing and 5 (1d10) poison
traps.description: A lever-operated pit trap that opens beneath creatures, causing them to fall onto poisoned spikes.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.133

traps.name: Magical Attraction
traps.trigger: Any metal object not being worn or carried that enters the room and weighs 150 pounds or less is instantly drawn to the shield. Any creature wearing or carrying metal items that enters the room or starts its turn there can feel the pull of the statue.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of transmutation magic over the shield.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 17) cast on the statue shuts down the attractive field for 1 hour. If the statue and shield are destroyed, the trap is disabled.

traps.effect: Any metal object that comes into direct contact with the shield disintegrates, showering the floor with powdered rust. Artifacts are immune to this corrosion. Any creature wearing or carrying metal items that enters the room or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check to resist the pull. On a failed check, the creature loses its footing, flies across the chamber, and slams into the statue, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it moved. If the character is wearing metal armor, the check is made with disadvantage.
traps.area: The hall containing the rusting statue of a knight at the west end
traps.description: A rusting statue of a knight gripping a large iron shield creates a magical field that attracts and disintegrates metal objects.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.134

traps.name: Gas Pocket
traps.trigger: If a torch, lantern, or other open flame is brought into the area, or if the secret door to area 10 is opened, the gas explodes.

detection.detail: The gas has a rotten odor.

disarm.detail: The explosion burns away the gas, which builds up again after 8 hours.

traps.effect: Each creature in the area of the gas pocket or within 15 feet of it must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failed save, or half damage on a successful one.
traps.area: The area of the gas pocket or within 15 feet of it
traps.description: This section of the underground river contains a buildup of flammable gas that has a rotten odor.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.135

traps.name: Trapped Chest
traps.trigger: Attempting to pick the lock.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of evocation magic around it.

disarm.detail: Picking the lock requires a successful DC 22 Dexterity check made using thieves' tools. This also disarms the lock's magical trap, allowing the chest to be opened safely.

traps.effect: If the check fails, the demon skull bites down on the thieves' tools and destroys them. If the check fails by 5 or more, the magical trap teleports the character making the check inside the locked chest, whereupon the character is restrained. The chains holding the chest then release it into the water, where it sinks to the bottom of the pool. Even if the chest is removed from the water, a character trapped within runs out of air after 5 rounds (see "Suffocating" in chapter 8 of the Player's Handbook).
traps.description: The chest is locked and doesn't appear to be trapped. However, a detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of evocation magic around it.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.135

traps.name: Stone Skull
traps.trigger: Each time a creature climbs through the skull's jaws, one of the flames in its eye sockets snuffs out. The third time a creature climbs through, the jaws clamp shut.

detection.detail: Any character searching the skull and succeeding on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check notes that the lower jaw is hinged.

disarm.method: jam a stout object into the skull's jaw
disarm.detail: A stout object jammed into the skull's jaw holds it open for as long as the object can withstand the damage.

traps.effect: The jaws clamp shut, making a melee weapon attack with a +10 bonus. On a hit, the target creature takes 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage and is grappled (escape DC 19). While it remains grappled, the creature takes 5 (1d10) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns. When that creature exits the jaws, the flames in the skull's eye sockets reignite, the jaws open, and the trap resets.
traps.description: A giant stone skull crusted with moss juts out from the end of the passageway. A flame flickers within each of its eye sockets, and a view into a chamber beyond can be seen through its open jaws.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.137

traps.name: Wind Tunnel Propeller
traps.trigger: whenever more than 20 pounds of pressure is placed on the corridor floor

detection.detail: a character discerns that the entire floor of the corridor is a single pressure plate

disarm.detail: While the propeller is motionless, a creature that isn't incapacitated can jam the mechanism with its body. When the propeller begins to turn, the creature must make a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check. If the check succeeds, the propeller is jammed until the start of the creature's next turn, when it can use its action to repeat the check. If the propeller is jammed for 3 consecutive rounds, it breaks down and becomes nonfunctional.

traps.effect: The adamantine propeller thunders into motion, spinning up to full speed in 6 seconds. While spinning up or slowing down, a creature can leap through a gap between two blades with a successful DC 20 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check; on a failed check, the character takes 33 (6d10) slashing damage. At full speed, the propeller deals 66 (12d10) slashing damage to any creature that passes through it, and the blades are turning too fast for a creature to leap between them. The rapidly spinning propeller also creates a wind tunnel effect, such that any creature that comes within 10 feet of the propeller or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw. A creature that fails the save is hurled northward into the pit in area 16. If this forced movement causes the creature to pass through the propeller, the creature takes damage from the spinning blades. One can jam the propeller by fixing an immovable rod in place between two of the blades. Other magic items wedged between the blades are knocked aside as the propeller turns. The propeller destroys all nonmagical objects lodged between its spinning blades. A creature that fails the check or chooses to extricate itself takes 11 (2d10) slashing damage and is ejected north of the propeller.
traps.description: A large adamantine propeller with five sharp blades blocks the passage. The entire floor is a pressure plate that activates the propeller.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.137

traps.name: Onyx Chest Trap
traps.trigger: Pushing the onyx button on Wongo's sarcophagus
traps.effect: forces any creature inside the onyx chest to succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 75 (10d6 + 40) force damage. A creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage turns to a pile of dust, leaving behind whatever gear it was holding or wearing.
traps.description: A trap within the onyx chest that triggers when the corresponding button on Wongo's sarcophagus is pressed.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.137

traps.name: Onyx Chest Button Trap
traps.trigger: Pushing the onyx button on the sarcophagus lid
traps.effect: Pushing the onyx button forces any creature inside the onyx chest to succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 75 (10d6 + 40) force damage. A creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage turns to a pile of dust, leaving behind whatever gear it was holding or wearing.
traps.description: A trap triggered by pressing the onyx button on the sarcophagus lid, affecting creatures inside the onyx chest.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.139

traps.name: Rusty Iron Chest Button Trap
traps.trigger: Pushing the rusty iron button on the sarcophagus lid
traps.effect: Pushing the rusty iron button causes any nonmagical metal objects inside the rusty iron chest (including objects carried or worn by a creature in the chest) to corrode into worthless piles of rust. Objects partly made of metal are ruined as their metal components decay.
traps.area: Nonmagical metal objects inside the rusty iron chest
traps.description: A trap triggered by pressing the rusty iron button on the sarcophagus lid, corroding metal objects inside the rusty iron chest.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.139

traps.name: Silver Chest Button Trap
traps.trigger: Pushing the silver button on the sarcophagus lid
traps.effect: Pushing the silver button causes any creature inside the silver chest to make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking 45 (10d8) cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.description: A trap triggered by pressing the silver button on the sarcophagus lid, affecting creatures inside the silver chest.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.139

traps.name: Slippery Ledge
traps.trigger: Taking damage while standing on the ledge
traps.effect: Any creature that takes damage while standing on the ledge must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall into the rift, plunging 100 feet into the water at area 64. The fall deals 35 (10d6) bludgeoning damage, or no damage with a successful DC 10 Dexterity saving throw.
traps.description: A slippery and uneven ledge that can cause creatures to fall into a rift.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.139

traps.name: False Tomb Trap
traps.trigger: If the illusory sunlight falling from the ceiling strikes the plaque when the coffin is opened, the stone block in the corridor outside the room slowly descends, sealing the entrance in 6 seconds.

detection.detail: A character who searches the tunnel spots the block with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: Casting dispel magic on the illusory sunlight dispels it and prevents the trap from triggering.

traps.effect: The stone block descends, sealing the entrance. A creature that wishes to enter or leave the tomb during this time can do so, moving up to its speed. If the creature ends its movement under the block, it must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. If the save succeeds, the creature manages to get out from under the block on the side it was moving toward. If the save fails, the creature takes 55 (10d10) bludgeoning damage. If this damage reduces the creature's hit points to 0, it is crushed to a pulp; otherwise, the creature is shoved into the room. The block is impervious to damage and spells. When fully lowered, the block is airtight and refuses to be budged. Four enormous cisterns filled with red wine are hidden in the walls behind the gargoyle heads. When the stone block seals off the entrance, the valves behind the heads open, causing the wine to pour from the gargoyles' mouths and nostrils. The wine floods the tomb at a rate of 1 foot per round. Trying to crawl into a gargoyle's mouth while wine is gushing out of it requires a successful DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check. As the wine begins pouring into the room, all creatures present must roll initiative. Track the passage of rounds: At the start of round 3, three wine weirds (use water weird statistics) flow into the tomb from the northwest, northeast, and southeast cisterns. The weirds attack anyone in the tomb and are invisible while fully immersed in wine. After 12 rounds, the wine fills the tomb. Use the underwater combat rules in chapter 9 of the Player's Handbook to handle fighting in these conditions. Visibility within the wine is limited to 5 feet. The ability to breathe water does not help a character drowning in wine. When 10 minutes have passed, the stone block sealing the tomb rises back up to its niche in the ceiling. The wine cascades down the west tunnel, pouring down the grand staircase (area 7). At dawn the next day, Withers sends tomb dwarves to clean up the room and tunnel, after which the wine cisterns magically refill and the trap resets.
traps.description: A trap in the False Tomb that seals the entrance with a stone block and floods the room with wine.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.141

traps.name: Alien Growth
traps.trigger: Any effect that deals fire, necrotic, or radiant damage destroys a patch of alien growth on contact.

detection.detail: The beholder's aberrant influence permeates the stonework across this level of the tomb, causing purple mold to sprout from the floors, walls, and ceilings. The mold smells like rotting corpses and occasionally releases clouds of harmless spores. As characters move through areas with alien growth, tiny eyeballs emerge from the mold to scrutinize them.

traps.effect: When a patch of growth is destroyed, the next nearest patch sprouts a stubby eyestalk that shoots a randomly determined eye ray at the nearest character. (Roll a d10 and consult the beholder stat block to determine which ray it produces.) After making this attack, the eyestalk quickly disappears back into the mold.
traps.description: The beholder's aberrant influence permeates the stonework across this level of the tomb, causing purple mold to sprout from the floors, walls, and ceilings.
traps.source: Tomb of Annihilation p.148

traps.name: Iron Barrier
traps.trigger: The barrier snaps down after 1 minute unless it is wedged in place with an iron spike, a stout weapon, or a similar object. Any creature underneath the sheet when it snaps shut is subject to the trap's effect.

detection.detail: Any character who examines the barrier discovers that it slides up into the ceiling.

disarm.detail: The barrier can be wedged in place with an iron spike, a stout weapon, or a similar object to prevent it from snapping down.

traps.effect: Any creature underneath the sheet when it snaps shut must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 44 (8d10) slashing damage. Any creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage is chopped in two.
traps.area: The crawlway blocked by the iron sheet.
traps.description: A 1-inch-thick, sharp-edged iron sheet etched with a snarling minotaur face blocks the crawlway. It can be lifted with a successful DC 17 Strength (Athletics) check, but snaps down after 1 minute unless wedged in place.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.??

traps.name: Curtain of Water
traps.trigger: Any creature passes through the curtain without a trident.

detection.detail: Radiates an aura of conjuration magic to a detect magic spell or similar effect.

disarm.detail: A successful dispel magic (DC 17) cast on the curtain causes it to vanish, leaving the archway open. The curtain magically reappears after 1 hour.

traps.effect: The water erupts as a fierce wave flowing north and south. Any creature in either hall is slammed by the water and must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the creature takes 14 (4d6) bludgeoning damage and is swept to the end of the hall with such great force that it falls prone. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw takes half damage and falls prone, but is not swept away.
traps.area: Both hallways connected by the curtain of water.
traps.description: A 1-foot-thick, 7-foot-high, 10-foot-wide curtain of clear water separates two hallways. Passing through with a trident is safe; without one, the water erupts into a fierce wave.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.??

traps.name: Rotating Crawlways
traps.trigger: When 50 pounds or more of weight is applied to the floor at the midpoint of tunnel A, a mechanism causes the tunnel to quickly rotate 90 degrees clockwise and sink 5 feet as it turns.

detection.detail: Any character searching for traps or secret doors in this tunnel notices a narrow seam in the stonework with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check. If the check succeeds by 5 or more, the character can deduce that the seam represents a point where two sections of tunnel can detach from one another.

traps.effect: Both ends of the tunnel are immediately cut off, trapping creatures inside. At the same time, a second crawlway perpendicular to the first (marked "Tunnel B" on map 5.3) rotates 90 degrees clockwise and sinks into place, positioned where tunnel A used to be. Characters who are flying, in gaseous form, or otherwise effectively weightless do not trigger the trap and can move through the tunnel safely. When tunnel B connects to the rest of the crawlway, a new passage running north to south is formed. Tunnel B is trapped similarly to tunnel A, except that both tunnels ascend 5 feet as they rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise when the trap triggers. The only way to return tunnel A to its original position is to trigger the trap from tunnel B, and vice versa. Characters trapped in a section of tunnel not connected to the rest of the crawlway have no clear means of escape. The tunnel is airtight. A single creature consumes the available air supply in 24 hours, with multiple creatures dividing that time up between them.
traps.area: 25-foot-long section of crawlway (Tunnel A) and a second crawlway (Tunnel B)
traps.description: A rotating crawlway trap that traps creatures inside an airtight tunnel.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.32

traps.name: Corrosive Gas Trap
traps.trigger: Removing the dial from its spoke inside the stone block releases a corrosive gas trapped within the block.

detection.detail: A character who searches for traps can detect the holes hidden behind the dial with a DC 25 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: Once found, these holes can be plugged with wax before the dial is removed, preventing the gas from escaping.

traps.effect: The gas escapes through tiny holes hidden behind the dial and fills the 5-foot space directly east of the block. Any creature in this area when the gas is released must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw, taking 44 (8d10) acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: 5-foot space directly east of the block
traps.description: A corrosive gas trap hidden behind a gold medallion and clay dial in area 35A.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.149

traps.name: Hieroglyphic Floor Trap
traps.trigger: Stepping on a floor tile that does not match the correct sequence of hieroglyphs.

detection.detail: The correct sequence is revealed by the clay dial in area 35A; no specific detection check is mentioned.

disarm.detail: Stepping on the tiles in the correct order disables the trap. After 24 hours, Withers sends 1d4 tomb dwarves to reset the trap.

traps.effect: When any creature steps on an incorrect floor tile, all four sphinx statues yawn and masses of magically summoned locusts fly out of their mouths. The locusts form a single cloud that fills a 15-foot cube centered above the offending floor tile. Each creature in the cloud when it forms, as well as any creature that enters the cloud for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, takes 44 (8d10) piercing damage. Any creature reduced to 0 hit points by this trap is killed and eaten to the bone by the devouring locusts.
traps.area: 15-foot cube centered above the offending floor tile
traps.description: A trap in area 35B that triggers when floor tiles are stepped on in the wrong order, summoning a cloud of locusts from sphinx statues.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.149

traps.name: Stone Block Ceiling Trap
traps.trigger: Stepping onto any floor tile in area 35B while the passage to the east is open causes the stone block at area 35A to rise and seal the tunnel.

detection.detail: No specific detection check is mentioned.

disarm.detail: No specific disarm method is mentioned.

traps.effect: Any creature atop the block when it meets the ceiling must succeed on a DC 7 Dexterity saving throw to leap clear in one direction or the other. On a failed save, the creature takes 55 (10d10) bludgeoning damage. Any creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage is crushed to a pulp. Otherwise, the creature falls prone inside the tomb.
traps.description: A trap where a stone block rises to seal a tunnel, potentially crushing creatures atop it.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.149

traps.name: Devouring Locusts
traps.trigger: Stepping on the offending floor tile
traps.effect: The locusts form a single cloud that fills a 15-foot cube centered above the offending floor tile. Each creature in the cloud when it forms, as well as any creature that enters the cloud for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, takes 44 (8d10) piercing damage. Any creature reduced to 0 hit points by this trap is killed and eaten to the bone by the devouring locusts. The cloud lasts for 1 minute or until another cloud of locusts is created.
traps.area: 15-foot cube centered above the offending floor tile
traps.description: A trap that releases a cloud of devouring locusts when a specific floor tile is stepped on.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.35

traps.name: Wailing Winds
traps.trigger: Pulling the lever on the west balcony

disarm.method: Returning the lever to its original up position
disarm.detail: Returning the lever to its original up position causes the winds to abate and the statue's fists to close.

traps.effect: Howling winds rise up and fill the room. While the winds are howling, any creature not standing on a floating platform that starts its turn in the room must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw or gain a random form of short-term madness, determined by rolling on the Short-Term Madness table in chapter 8 of the Dungeon Master's Guide. Constructs and undead are immune to this madness. In addition, the winds cause creatures in the room to suffer disadvantage on all Strength-based skill checks, including checks made to jump to and from the floating platforms and checks made to climb the walls.
traps.description: A trap triggered by a lever that fills the room with howling winds causing madness and hindering Strength checks.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.35

traps.name: Revolving Room Trap
traps.trigger: Pulling the iron lever in area 38A activates the trap in area 38C.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

traps.effect: Three hidden locks seal the south door, a wall of stone spell blocks the rectangular hole in the ceiling (cutting off escape to area 38B), and the room begins revolving. Any creature that is not firmly attached to a wall, flying, or under the effect of a gaseous form spell or similar magic is knocked about the revolving room. The creature must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw at the start of each of its turns, taking 11 (2d10) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.area: The revolving room (area 38C) and the rectangular hole in the ceiling.
traps.description: A trap that revolves a cylindrical room, knocking creatures about and dealing bludgeoning damage.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.152

traps.name: Revolving Room
traps.trigger: The room revolves, knocking about any creature not firmly attached to a wall, flying, or under the effect of a gaseous form spell or similar magic.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: The room stops tumbling if the lever in area 38A is raised, or if the south door is opened or destroyed. The door's locks are hidden in the walls and can't be picked with thieves' tools, and it takes three separate knock spells to unlock them. The door can also be wrenched open with a successful DC 26 Strength (Athletics) check or attacked. It has AC 17; 50 hit points; and immunity to fire, piercing, poison, psychic, slashing, and thunder damage.

traps.effect: At the start of each of its turns, a creature in the room must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 11 (2d10) bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. While the room is revolving, an additional effect is triggered at the end of initiative count 10. Roll a d20 and consult the Revolving Room Effects table.
traps.description: A revolving room that knocks creatures about and triggers random effects.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.153

traps.name: Revolving Room Effects
traps.trigger: Triggered at the end of initiative count 10 while the room is revolving.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

traps.effect: Roll a d20 and consult the Revolving Room Effects table: 1-6: The demon faces exhale jets of a soporific gas that dissipates quickly. Each creature in the room that is not immune to the poisoned condition must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or fall unconscious. An unconscious creature can repeat the saving throw each time it takes damage, ending the effect on itself on a success. 7-12: The demon faces exhale jets of sparkling dust, which blind any creature in the room that does not succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. A creature's blindness lasts until it is cured with a lesser restoration spell or similar magic. 13-18: Stone spikes 6 inches long magically protrude from the walls. Any creature that takes damage from the room at the start of its turn takes an additional 11 (2d10) piercing damage from the spikes. The spikes retract when the next room effect is triggered. 19-20: The demon faces spew jets of an incendiary gas that promptly ignites, filling the room with fire. Each creature in the room takes 45 (10d8) fire damage.
traps.description: Random effects triggered by the revolving room.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.153

traps.name: Golem Pit
traps.trigger: Entering the area or manipulating the statues.

detection.detail: Either statue can be identified with a successful DC 12 Intelligence (Religion) check. A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of abjuration magic around each statue.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

traps.effect: An invisible wall of force covers the top of the pit. By manipulating the statues, characters can teleport the golem up to their level, or send one of their own into the pit. Rotating the statue of Azuth to the right teleports one creature inside the pit onto the third plinth. Rotating the statue of Torm to the right teleports anything on or above the third plinth into the pit. The clay golem has orders to attack any creature that it sees and can reach.
traps.description: A pit containing a clay golem and a stone chest, with statues that teleport creatures.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.153

traps.name: Stone Chest
traps.trigger: Opening the chest by any means other than the silver key.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: A character using thieves' tools can pick the lock with a successful DC 20 Dexterity check.

traps.effect: Releases a cloud of gas that fills a 15-foot cube centered above the chest (filling the entire pit). The gas instantly corrodes and destroys all nonmagical metal that comes into contact with it, including armor and weapons. Metal objects sealed in containers are protected.
traps.description: A stone chest that releases a corrosive gas if opened without the silver key.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.153

traps.name: Sarcophagus Arcane Lock Trap
traps.trigger: Opening the sarcophagus by any means other than the ritual

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals auras of abjuration and evocation magic around the sarcophagus.

disarm.detail: Can be opened with a knock spell or forced open with a successful DC 25 Strength (Athletics) check, but doing so triggers the trap.

traps.effect: A prismatic spray spell (save DC 19) erupts from the wall behind the sarcophagus. All creatures in the room, as well as creatures in the narrow hallway to the south, become targets of the spell.
traps.area: All creatures in the room, as well as creatures in the narrow hallway to the south
traps.description: The sarcophagus lid is sealed shut with an arcane lock spell. If opened by any means other than the ritual, a prismatic spray spell erupts.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.43

traps.name: Wraith Ambush
traps.trigger: Performing any of the ritual actions incorrectly
traps.effect: Three wraiths rise from the bones on the floor. The wraiths attack until they are destroyed and pursue any characters who flee this area. When the wraiths appear, any character wearing one of the frog masks is polymorphed into a frog, as though it had failed a saving throw against the polymorph spell.
traps.description: If any ritual actions are performed incorrectly, three wraiths rise from the bones on the floor and attack.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.43

traps.name: Third Curtain of the Feast Hall
traps.trigger: Any creature that looks at this curtain

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of enchantment magic radiating from the third curtain.

traps.effect: Any creature that looks at this curtain must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of it. A frightened creature tries to leave the room as quickly as possible and cannot reenter. Once outside the room, a creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that saves against this effect is unaffected by the curtain thereafter and can reenter the room.
traps.description: An enchanted curtain that frightens creatures that look upon it.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.43

traps.name: Lord of the Feast (Severed Boar's Head)
traps.trigger: Any humanoid that can see the severed boar's head

detection.detail: The rotting head of a giant boar is mounted to the wall behind the final curtain. Fresh blood and gore spatters its tusks, dribbling down the wall beneath it.

disarm.detail: Destroying the Lord of the Feast ends its charm effect on all creatures. The boar's head is a Medium object with AC 5 and 22 hit points.

traps.effect: Any humanoid that can see the severed boar's head must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by it. On its turn, a charmed creature does nothing except approach the severed head and put its own head in the boar's mouth. Only one head can fit in the mouth at a time. If the boar's mouth is already full, a charmed creature waits patiently until the mouth is clear. Any creature that ends its turn with its head in the boar's mouth takes 22 (4d10) slashing damage as the boar's jaws clamp down. If this damage reduces the creature to 0 hit points, it is decapitated. A charmed creature can repeat the saving throw each time it takes damage, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once a creature successfully saves against this effect, it cannot be affected by the boar's head for 24 hours.
traps.area: Line of sight to the boar's head
traps.description: A severed boar's head that charms humanoids into placing their heads in its mouth, clamping down and decapitating them.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.43

traps.name: Slick Vault Floor
traps.trigger: Any creature that steps onto or starts its turn on the floor

detection.detail: The floor beneath the dome is magically slick.

traps.effect: Any creature that steps onto or starts its turn on the floor must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. When an untethered creature is shoved or otherwise moved across the floor, it travels in one direction and does not stop until it comes into contact with a wall or other barrier.
traps.area: The floor beneath the dome in the Vault of the Beholder
traps.description: A magically slick floor that causes creatures to fall prone and slide uncontrollably.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.44

traps.name: Lava Trap
traps.trigger: Molten lava begins pouring from the tiny holes in the ceiling as soon as any character comes within 1 foot of the candle or removes it from the sconce.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified.

traps.effect: The lava rains down and magically drains away through the holes in the floor. Each creature in the cell when the lava begins to fall must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Any creature that enters the cell for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must repeat the saving throw. Because of the cell's antimagic field, magic items and spells that provide resistance to fire offer no protection here.
traps.description: A trap that pours molten lava from ceiling holes when the candle is approached or removed.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.159

traps.name: Flood Trap
traps.trigger: The water begins to pour into the cell through rows of tiny holes in the ten-foot-high ceiling when characters appear in the cell.

detection.detail: No detection method specified.

disarm.detail: Trying to stuff or block the holes doesn't stop the water from pouring in.

traps.effect: The water fills the cell at a rate of 1 foot per round, taking 10 rounds to fill the room. If the candle is left in its sconce, the rising water extinguishes it on the fourth round. Because of the cell's antimagic field, spells and magic items that enable characters to breathe underwater don't function here. Any character who runs out of air begins to suffocate.
traps.description: A trap that floods the cell with water, risking suffocation.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.159

traps.name: Falling Sand Pit Trap
traps.trigger: The falling sand fills the room at a rate of 6 inches per round. If the sand reaches a depth of 12 inches, the floor splits open along its seam.

detection.detail: Any character who searches the cell and succeeds on a DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) check notices a seam running down the middle of the floor from north to south.

disarm.detail: No disarm method specified. Characters can stuff holes with cloth or wax to slow the sand by 1 inch per round.

traps.effect: When the pit opens, half of the floor swings down to the west and the other half drops to the east, and the sand stops falling. A 6-inch-wide ledge surrounds the pit on all sides. Any creature standing on the floor when it opens must make a DC 15 Dexterity check; those standing along the walls have advantage on the check. On a successful save, a creature finds purchase on the ledge. A creature that fails the save falls. The 10-foot-deep pit contains two giant stone rollers with interlocking stone teeth. Anything larger than a grain of sand gets chewed up between these rollers, taking 132 (24d10) force damage. Any creature reduced to 0 hit points by this damage is ground to a pulp. A creature that passes through the rollers with at least 1 hit point remaining lands on an iron grate 5 feet below the grinders. A stone button is set into one of the walls above the grate and is visible only to creatures under the rollers. When pressed, the button causes the rollers to stop turning and retract into the walls, allowing creatures that survived the horrid trap to climb out with a successful DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.
traps.description: A pit trap in a cell where sand fills the room, eventually causing the floor to split open and drop creatures into a pit with grinding stone rollers.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.160

traps.name: Sphere of Annihilation in Devil Face
traps.trigger: Any character who stands within 5 feet of the sphere can hear a faint whisper emanating from it.

detection.detail: A successful DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) check allows a character to make out words in Abyssal that translate as follows: "Darkness is coming for you. Your doom is at hand."

disarm.detail: The sphere of annihilation can't be controlled or moved.

traps.effect: The darkness within the mouth is a sphere of annihilation, which can't be controlled or moved.
traps.description: A green stone face of devilish countenance protrudes from the wall. The devil's mouth is agape and filled with darkness. The devil face is 6 feet tall, with a mouth 2 feet in diameter. A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals an aura of transmutation magic on the face.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.162

traps.name: Mirror of Life Trapping
traps.trigger: Any creature within 30 feet of the mirror that sees its reflection

detection.detail: Casting an identify spell on the mirror reveals its command words and magical properties.

disarm.detail: Speaking the word "Khomara" while standing within 5 feet of the mirror deactivates or reactivates it.

traps.effect: Any creature within 30 feet of the mirror that sees its reflection must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be imprisoned within one of the mirror's twelve extradimensional cells, along with anything it is wearing or carrying. Constructs automatically succeed on the saving throw.
traps.description: This dusty room is fifteen feet square and empty except for an ornate, rectangular mirror mounted on the wall opposite the room's only exit. Attached to the west wall with sovereign glue is a mirror of life trapping.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.162

traps.name: Golden Sun
traps.trigger: Whenever the sun or its chain are touched or damaged, the sun's smile fades to an inscrutable expression, and it emits tremendous heat in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on itself. The first time the queen's remains or any of her treasures are removed from the sarcophagus, the sun's expression turns angry as it emits rays of searing light.

detection.detail: A detect magic spell or similar effect reveals auras of evocation magic around the golden sun.

disarm.detail: The sun and its chain are treated as a single Small object with AC 15; 22 hit points; and immunity to fire, poison, and psychic damage. The sun loses its magical properties when it shoots its rays or is destroyed.

traps.effect: Any creature that starts its turn in the area takes 10 (3d6) fire damage. This effect ends if all creatures leave the affected area. When the queen's remains or treasures are removed, each creature within 30 feet of the sun that doesn't have total cover against it must succeed on a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or be struck by a ray, which deals 42 (12d6) fire damage.
traps.area: 20-foot-radius sphere centered on the sun; 30 feet for rays
traps.description: A two-foot-diameter orb hanging from a chain above the sarcophagus, made of hammered gold to resemble a smiling sun. It emits tremendous heat when touched or damaged, and shoots searing rays when the queen's remains or treasures are removed.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.53

traps.name: Napaka's Baleful Gas
traps.trigger: If the scepter is removed and not immediately replaced with its nonmagical twin from area 52, or if Napaka's remains are removed from their resting place, the queen's corpse opens its mouth in a wide yawn and exhales a baleful black gas.

disarm.detail: Replacing the scepter with its nonmagical twin from area 52, or not removing Napaka's remains, prevents the trap.

traps.effect: The gas fills a 15-foot cube centered on the corpse. Each creature in the area must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw, taking 45 (7d12) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
traps.description: A magical trap triggered by removing Napaka's scepter or remains, causing her corpse to exhale a baleful black gas.
traps.source: Tomb of the Nine Gods p.53

traps.name: Rolling Doom (Granite Ball)
traps.trigger: When the chest or its lid is lifted, a heavy stone ball tumbles down the stairs.

detection.detail: Finding the compartment requires that a character search the tunnel ceiling and succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check.

disarm.detail: The hatch can be jammed with an iron spike or with a successful DC 20 Dexterity check made using thieves' tools.

traps.effect: When released, the stone ball thunders down the stairs and tumbles into the pit at 54C. Any character on the stairs or in the tunnel below can stay ahead of the ball by running toward the pit. A character can also leap over the ball with a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. Any character who fails the check or can't move out of the ball's way is struck for 22 (4d10) bludgeoning damage and knocked prone.
